en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Ārāmavagga 58.
The Training Rule on Exhortation:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodha Monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, having approached the nuns' quarters, were instructing the group-of-six nuns.
The nuns said this to the group-of-six nuns:
"Come, noble ladies, let us go for the instruction."
“Venerable lady, even if we were to go for the sake of the exhortation, the Venerable Chabbaggiyā bhikkhunīs would come right here and exhort us.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the Chabbaggiyā bhikkhunīs not go for the exhortation?”... [and so on].
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs do not go for the exhortation?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs not go for the exhortation?
This, monks, is neither for the pleasing of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence...
And so, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: ‘If a bhikkhunī, when she has been invited by a bhikkhu to go for the exhortation, should not go, it is an offense of wrong-doing.’"
“Whatever nun, however, should not go for the exhortation or for the communal living, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"Bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the "bhikkhunī" intended in this context.
"Exhortation" (ovāda) means:
The eight *garudhammas*.
"Living together" means:
a common formal act, a common recitation of the Pātimokkha, and training in common.
If one simply lays down the burden, thinking, "I will not go for the sake of instruction or for communal living," there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
There is no offense if there is an obstacle.
If, having sought one, she does not obtain a companion nun,
in the case of illness or in times of distress.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of one who is a first-offender.
The eighth training rule is concluded.
